title: Reduced State Stabilizer Rényi Entropy as a Probe of Quantum Phase Transitions in Frustrated J_1-J_2 Spin Models
authors: George Biswas, Santanu Sarkar, Jun-Yi Wu, Anindya Biswas
abstract: We investigate whether the second-order purity-corrected stabilizer Rényi entropy (SRE) of reduced two-qubit density matrices can serve as a reliable local indicator of quantum phase transitions (QPTs) in frustrated quantum spin systems. We consider the one-dimensional isotropic \(J_1-J_2\) Heisenberg model, the one-dimensional XXZ \(J_1-J_2\) model, and the two-dimensional \(J_1-J_2\) Heisenberg model on a \(4\times4\) square lattice. Unlike several previously studied quantum information measures, which fail to detect QPTs in the ground state of these frustrated systems, the reduced ground-state purity-corrected SRE successfully identifies most transitions. For the remaining cases, we consider a low temperature subjacent state, modeled as a statistical mixture of the ground and first excited states with a Maxwell--Boltzmann-type occupation probability. For the 1D isotropic model, the subjacent-state SRE shows a discontinuity at the critical point, yielding \(α_c(\infty)=0.24116\), in excellent agreement with established values; the ground-state SRE shows a point of inflection, yielding \(α_c(\infty)=0.2681\). For the 1D XXZ model, the subjacent-state SRE reproduces the full anisotropy dependent phase diagram, while the ground-state SRE captures transitions only at low anisotropy. For the 2D model, the subjacent-state SRE detects two transitions, at \(α_c(4\times4)=0.40781\) and \(0.6208\), while the ground-state SRE identifies the second at \(0.6230\). Compared with conventional two-qubit entanglement, purity-corrected SRE shows a clear advantage in revealing otherwise-invisible phase transitions, establishing it as a robust, efficient, local probe of frustrated quantum criticality.
summary: This work tests the utility of the purity-corrected stabilizer Rényi entropy (SRE) as a local probe for Quantum Phase Transitions in frustrated spin models. By applying the SRE to 1D and 2D $J_1-J_2$ spin systems, the authors demonstrate that this measure is highly effective, often succeeding where other quantum information measures fail. The results establish the purity-corrected SRE as a robust diagnostic tool for quantum criticality.
main_problem: To determine if the purity-corrected stabilizer Rényi entropy (SRE) of reduced two-qubit density matrices can serve as a reliable local indicator for Quantum Phase Transitions (QPTs) in frustrated quantum spin systems.
main_result: The purity-corrected SRE successfully identifies most QPTs in the studied models, showing a clear advantage over conventional entanglement measures in revealing otherwise-invisible phase transitions.
method: The study uses the purity-corrected SRE calculated from reduced two-qubit density matrices, comparing ground-state results with those derived from a low-temperature subjacent state (a statistical mixture of the ground and first excited states).
model_or_system: The analysis investigates frustrated quantum spin-$ rac{1}{2}$ models, specifically the one-dimensional isotropic and XXZ $J_1-J_2$ Heisenberg models, and the two-dimensional $J_1-J_2$ Heisenberg model on a square lattice.
key_observables: Purity-corrected Stabilizer Rényi Entropy (SRE) of reduced two-qubit density matrices; critical exponents ($\alpha_c(\infty)$).
important_parameters: Frustration parameter ($\alpha = J_2/J_1$); lattice dimensionality (1D vs 2D); temperature regime (ground state vs. subjacent state).
main_assumptions: The system is modeled by a subjacent state at low, finite temperatures, which is a statistical mixture of the ground and first excited states. The analysis relies on reduced two-qubit density matrices.
paper_structure: The paper introduces the diagnostic tool (purity-corrected SRE) and applies it systematically to three different frustrated spin models (1D isotropic, 1D XXZ, 2D Heisenberg), comparing ground-state results against subjacent-state results to test the robustness of the indicator.
why_interesting: The use of quantum information measures like SRE to probe critical points in strongly correlated magnetic systems provides a novel, local diagnostic tool that complements traditional thermodynamic or entanglement-based methods.

figures.caption: FIG. 1. Concurrence and negativity of the reduced two-qubit ground state for the J1 −J2 Heisenberg models. (a) One- dimensional model (N = 16). (b) Two-dimensional model (N = 4 × 4). In both cases, the bipartite entanglement measures fail to display clear signatures of the quantum phase transitions. In the two-dimensional model, both concurrence and negativity vanish for α ≳0.57.

FIG. 2. Reduced two-qubit stabilizer Rényi entropy f M2 of the ground state for the one-dimensional isotropic J1 −J2 Heisen- berg model with system sizes N = 20, 24. The purity-corrected SRE varies smoothly with the frustration parameter α and ex- hibits a distinct change in curvature near the known quantum critical point. The right inset shows the corresponding deriva- tive, whose peak identiﬁes the location of the curvature change. The left inset presents the ﬁnite-size scaling of the peak posi- tions, αc(N), by plotting ln[αc(N) −αc(∞)] versus ln N for N = 12, 16, 20, 24. A linear ﬁt yields the thermodynamic criti- cal point αc(∞) = 0.2681 and a scaling exponent of 1.6536.

FIG. 3. Reduced two-qubit stabilizer Rényi entropy f M2 of the subjacent mixture of the ground state and the ﬁrst excited-state for the one-dimensional isotropic J1 −J2 Heisenberg model as a function of the frustration parameter α, for N = 20 and N = 24. In both cases, f M2 exhibits a discontinuity near the quantum critical point. The inset shows the ﬁnite-size scaling of ln[αc(N) −αc(∞)] versus ln N for N = 12, 16, 20, 24, yield- ing αc(∞) = 0.24116 and slope 1.9601.

FIG. 4. Reduced two-qubit concurrence and negativity of the subjacent mixture of the ground state and the ﬁrst excited-state for the one-dimensional isotropic J1−J2 Heisenberg model with N = 16. Both quantities exhibit clear nonanalytic signatures near the known quantum critical point.
